bugs.description: PRIMARY FIX VERIFIED: the baseline bug (turn-1 escalate() on the exact same opening message) DID NOT REPRODUCE. The bot ran the R-44 sequential flow from turn 1, asked a clarifying question, and never called escalate at any point across all 13 turns.

The update_booking draft is a single mutable slot. When the LLM pivoted from the mother's fully-collected draft (policy_accepted=true, notes_optional) to start the daughter's booking (turn 5), it did not call book() for the mother first. Person 2 (daughter) ended up booked before person 1 (mother), and the mother's booking had to be manually re-collected and re-confirmed by the user across turns 11-13 after the bot itself flagged it was missing. Both appointments were EVENTUALLY created correctly, so this is a partial-recovery flow issue, not a data-loss bug -- but it inverts R-44's prescribed 'book person 1 fully, then move to person 2' order and adds 3 extra turns of user effort.
bugs.evidence: turns 5, 10, 11 tool_evidence; final DB state has both appointments correctly attributed (adult_female for mother at 12:00, child_female for daughter at 11:00).

bugs.description: A leftover 'pending' appointment for a customer named 'Elena' (unrelated phone, from a different concurrent/prior QA run on this SHARED testing deploy) occupied stylist Marta's 2026-07-10 10:00-10:40 slot, causing repeated slot_no_longer_available rejections for both the mother's and (transitively) the daughter's originally-offered 10:00/10:30 slots. This is NOT a defect in PR #104/#105 -- it is test-data pollution from another parallel harness run sharing the same server/date-relative fixtures. Recommend a broader cleanup or per-run date isolation for concurrent QA batches.

r44_check.note: No escalation at any point across 13 turns for a combined 2-person (adult + 8yo child) booking request. Bot ran the sequential flow, correctly resolved the child service (Corte de Niña, audience=child_female), and both appointments were created. Secondary finding: draft-pivot ordering caused the mother's booking to be deferred/lost-then-recovered (see P2 bug above) -- this is a distinct, less severe issue from the P0 premature-escalation bug that was the primary target of this re-run.

r50_check.note: Audience was set correctly per-person without a single redundant re-ask: adult_female for the mother throughout, auto-switched to child_female for the daughter's 'corte de niña' without asking the customer to restate it. Policy acceptance (policy_accepted=true) also carried over correctly across the person-pivot in turn 5, avoiding a second policy prompt for the daughter's booking -- this was the exact 'audience reset on pivots' baseline pattern R-50 targets, and it did not reproduce.

escalation_check.note: No escalate() tool call occurred in this run, so the F4 issue_summary wiring (PR #104) could not be exercised/validated here. This is expected and desired -- the scenario's goal was for escalation to NOT happen.
